text.tspan: Quick questions, asked while Spark builds. Spark Assist invites each user to tell us who
they are. Every suggestion fits them, not our assumptions.

g.text: Spark Assist asks one question at a time while the user waits

text.tspan: Unity Spark lets anyone make the game they have in their head. We can expect a wide variety of
users, from casual gamers to experienced developers. Unity Spark needs to understand every user’s
interests, understanding and communication style to provide the best possible experience and keep
them engaged.
38% of people who drop off before getting something playable leave during the first build
(median 8 min 50 s), with nothing to keep them engaged.
User sessions show users with wildly different backgrounds and skill levels. Each type of user
needs a different level of support and prompting.
Short prompts lead to generic games: 60% of first prompts are under 10 words, and users say
the result “felt like someone else’s game”.
Spark Assist asks quick questions while Spark builds and makes changes, turning waiting time into
something useful. Each answer builds a profile that shapes the suggestions Spark makes, so the
game feels like theirs. Users can review and edit their profile from their account page.
Spark Assist asks questions during builds and
changes, starting with the four core questions
Skip, Not now and Don’t ask again
Answers editable on the Account page
Answers rank next steps and pitch new projects
New questions added over time, with old
answers that expire or resurface as users
change. The AI team uses the profile to
further improve the quality of responses for
each individual.
More people sticking around long enough to get something playable, and through each step of the
funnel after that. We’d also expect the end result to be better suited to each user’s ideas and
preferences.

g.text: Prompt to playable rises from 57% to 65%
Fewer drop-offs during the first build (now 38%)
Share of users who answer a question, and average answered
Share of suggested next steps chosen with “Do this next”
Low dismiss rate; time to first playable unchanged

text.tspan: We’ll A/B test it for four weeks: Spark Assist on versus off for new users.
Some users may find the questions annoying or distracting, so they sit beside build progress and
can be dismissed, then turned back on from their profile. Others may worry about what we store,
so answers are optional, visible, editable and only used inside Spark.
